sentences.text: learn English for everyday situations. Today, we have an important and useful topic, how
to speak English at a train station. If you travel by train, you may need to buy a ticket,
ask for directions, find the right platform, and understand train announcements. If you
don't speak English well, this can feel stressful. But don't worry. In this episode, I will teach
you simple and useful English phrases to help you feel more confident at the train station.
In this episode, you will learn how to, one, buy a train ticket, two, ask about train times,
three, find the right platform, four, ask for help in directions, five, understand train announcements,
six, communicate on the train, seven, use polite expressions at the train station. By the end of
this episode, you will feel more comfortable speaking English when traveling by train. Let's get
started. Buying a train ticket. When you arrive at the train station, you first need to buy a
ticket. You can buy a ticket at the ticket counter or from a ticket machine. At the ticket counter,
hello, I'd like to buy a ticket to London, please. How much is a ticket to Manchester? I need a
one-way ticket. One way equals only going, no return. I need a return ticket. Return equals
going and coming back. Can I have a ticket for the 10 a.m. train? Do you have any discounts for
students slash seniors? At the ticket machine, select your destination. Choose one way or return.
Insert your payment. Press OK to confirm. Example conversation. Hello, I'd like to buy a ticket to
Oxford, please. Sure, one way or return. Return, please. That will be 25 pounds. Here is your ticket.
Thank you. Tip. If you don't know which ticket to buy, you can ask, what's the cheapest ticket?
Can I buy my ticket online? Asking for train times. You need to know when your train leaves and arrives.
Common questions. What time is the next train to Edinburgh? When does the train to Birmingham leave?
What time will we arrive in Bristol? Is the 5 p.m. train on time? Is there a train at night?
Example conversation. Excuse me, what time is the next train to Cambridge? The next train leaves at
3.30 p.m. Thank you. Tip. If you want to ask if your train is late, say, is the train delayed?
How long is the delay? Finding the right platform. After buying your ticket, you need to find the
correct platform. Common questions. Which platform does the train to Glasgow leave from? Where is
platform 5? Is this the right platform for the train to Liverpool? Do I need to change trains?
Example conversation. Excuse me, where is platform 3? It's that way on your left. Thank you. Tip,
platforms are usually numbered. One, two, three, etc. Look for signs or screens to check the
platform number. Asking for help. If you feel lost, don't worry. You can ask for help. Common
phrases. Excuse me, can you help me? I think I'm lost. Where is the ticket counter? Is this the right
train to Newcastle? How do I get to platform 7? Excuse me, is this the train to Brighton? Staff.
No, this train goes to Bristol. The Brighton train is on platform 4. Oh, thank you so much.
Understanding train announcements. At the train station, you will hear announcements about train
arrivals, delays, and platform changes. Common announcements. The train to Manchester is arriving
on platform 6. The 4.15 train to Glasgow is delayed by 10 minutes. Attention passengers.
The train to Birmingham has been cancelled. Listen carefully and check the electronic boards for
updates. Communicating on the train. When you are on the train, you might need to talk to other
passengers or train staff. Common phrases. Excuse me, is this seat taken? Can I put my bag here?
How long is the journey? Where is the next stop? Excuse me, where is the toilet?
Example conversation. Excuse me, is this seat free? No, sorry, my friend is sitting here.
Oh, okay, thank you. Using polite expressions at the train station.
Being polite is important in English. Here are some useful polite phrases.
Saying, thank you. Thank you for your help. I really appreciate it.
Saying, sorry, I'm sorry. I don't understand. Sorry, can you repeat that?
Asking politely, could you help me please? Excuse me, may I ask you something?
Now, you know how to speak English at the train station. Final tips.
One, arrive early so you have time to find your platform.
Two, check the departure boards for train times and platform numbers.
Three, ask for help if you are lost or confused.
Four, listen carefully to announcements.
Five, be polite and use please and thank you.
I hope this episode helps you feel confident when traveling by train.
